key_insight: Relit-LiVE jointly learns an "environment video" representation together with a neural renderer, removing the need for fragile per-frame intrinsic decomposition and enabling temporally consistent, realistic relighting of real-world videos.
problem_solved: Existing video relighting pipelines rely on accurate intrinsic decomposition (albedo, normals, illumination) which is unreliable for in-the-wild videos and causes distorted appearance, broken material rendering, and accumulated temporal artifacts during relighting.
method: Jointly learn a compact environment-video representation that captures scene illumination dynamics instead of depending on per-frame intrinsic decomposition.

Train a neural rendering/diffusion-based video renderer conditioned on the learned environment video to perform forward rendering under novel lighting while enforcing temporal coherence and appearance regularization.
Optimize the environment video and renderer end-to-end so the learned illumination cues and rendering model compensate for imperfect intrinsic estimates and reduce temporal artifacts.
impact: Provides a practical, robust approach for relighting real-world videos with improved realism and temporal stability, lowering the bar for applications in VFX, AR/VR, video editing, and dataset augmentation without requiring perfect intrinsic decomposition.
visual_elements: Before / after relighting frame pairs (real-world video examples) to show quality and material preservation
Pipeline diagram: input video → joint environment-video learning loop → conditioned neural renderer → relit video
Visualization of the learned environment video (sequence of environment maps or light probes) to illustrate how illumination evolves
Temporal-consistency comparison chart or frame-difference heatmaps vs baseline methods to highlight reduced flicker/artifacts
paper_title: Relit-LiVE: Relight Video by Jointly Learning Environment Video
paper_authors: Weiqing Xiao, Hong Li, Xiuyu Yang, Houyuan Chen, Wenyi Li
